title: Vanishing / Exploding Gradients
interviewAnswer: Repeated multiplication through deep networks can shrink or amplify gradients. Initialization, normalization, ReLU-like activations, residual connections and gradient clipping help depending on the architecture.
why: Gradient pathologies explain why older deep networks were hard to train and motivate ReLU, residual connections, normalization and clipping.
intuition: Backprop multiplies many local derivatives. If most are below 1, gradients shrink toward zero; if large, gradients can blow up.
deepDive: Sigmoid/tanh saturation can produce tiny derivatives; recurrent multiplication across long sequences intensifies the effect. Exploding gradients cause unstable updates/NaNs. Initialization preserves signal variance; ReLU-like activations reduce saturation; residual connections provide shorter identity paths; normalization stabilizes scales; gradient clipping caps extreme norms.
math: For a chain, ∂L/∂h_0 = Π_l (∂h_l/∂h_{l-1}) · ∂L/∂h_L; repeated singular values <1 shrink and >1 amplify.
workedExample: If early layers show near-zero gradient norms while late layers learn, inspect saturation/initialization and consider residual/norm architecture rather than only increasing learning rate.
commonMistakes: Using gradient clipping as a cure for every optimization problem.
Ignoring NaNs from data/loss even when gradients explode.
production: Track gradient norms/NaNs in training telemetry and checkpoint before instability so long GPU runs can be diagnosed/resumed.
